move: twelve mirrored wedges of drifting gradient discs turn as a kaleidoscope
how: A 520px offscreen canvas draws four additive radial-gradient discs moving on sines (one and two cycles per loop). The main canvas clips 12 wedges around centre, mirrors every other one, rotates the whole pattern two wedges per loop, and inside each wedge counter-rotates the source a full turn and slides it one tile (520px) per loop before filling with a repeating pattern of the source, so t=D is identical to t=0. A radial vignette darkens the edges and a static caption sits bottom-left.
adapt: Change the four disc colour pairs, the source background and N wedges; keep the two-wedge spin, the full counter-rotation and the one-tile slide so the loop closes.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and caption; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one {t:0->D, ease:none} tween whose onUpdate runs the seek paint. Canvas is fixed 1280x720.
caveats: createPattern and 12 clipped 7x-tile fills per frame are moderate cost
catalog says rotating patterns; the pattern is mirrored wedges of a canvas, not CSS gradients
